title: What Does Animal Re-Identification Learn? Linear Biological Concepts and Their Origins in Visual Representations
abstract: arXiv:2609.06020v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Conservation increasingly relies on camera traps that collect more wildlife imagery than experts can manually analyze, making animal re-identification (Re-ID) essential for monitoring individuals and populations. Yet understanding which cues drive model decisions is challenging for ViT-based Re-ID models, whose metric-learning objectives provide no explicit supervision for biological concepts. We ask whether such models nonetheless organize their representations along biologically meaningful axes. Using a DINOv3 backbone fine-tuned for Western lowland gorilla Re-ID with triplet-margin loss, we find that sex and age emerge as linear directions that generalize to held-out individuals, reaching up to 0.91 AUROC and being recoverable from a single image per individual. translated_title: 动物重识别学到了什么？线性生物学概念及其在视觉表征中的起源
translated_abstract: 保护工作越来越依赖相机陷阱收集的野生动物图像，其数量已超出专家人工分析的能力，因此动物重识别（Re-ID）对监测个体和种群至关重要。然而，对于基于ViT的重识别模型而言，理解哪些线索驱动模型决策颇具挑战，因为其度量学习目标并未对生物学概念提供显式监督。我们探究这类模型是否仍会沿着具有生物学意义的轴来组织其表征。通过使用以三元组边界损失微调的DINOv3骨干网络进行西部低地大猩猩重识别，我们发现性别和年龄作为线性方向涌现出来，这些方向能泛化到未见过的个体，AUROC最高可达0.91，并且可以从每个个体的单张图像中恢复出来。激活引导实验进一步表明，性别方向被模型因果性地使用，能够将相当比例的预测翻转为相反的性别。（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该研究发现，在大猩猩重识别模型的视觉表征中，性别和年龄等生物学概念会自发地以线性方向的形式涌现，并通过激活引导实验证明模型在预测中因果性地使用了这些生物学方向。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that biological concepts such as sex and age spontaneously emerge as linear directions in the visual representations of gorilla re-identification models, and activation steering experiments demonstrate that the model causally uses these biological directions in its predictions.
